about: Summaries of the demonstration Employee Policy Handbook v1.0 (fictional Example Organisation Ltd). The full handbook is not stored in Alice: it stays in the policy library folder, and each summary points to its section.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Annual leave
summaries.text:
Full-time staff get 25 days' paid annual leave plus the 8 usual bank and public holidays (Scotland and Northern Ireland use their own holidays, same total). Part-time staff get a pro rata amount. Entitlement rises by one day after 5 years' service and another after 10 years (maximum 27 days plus bank holidays). The leave year runs 1 April to 31 March and never falls below the statutory 5.6 weeks.

Booking: request through the HR system with at least twice the length of the leave as notice (two weeks' notice for one week off). Managers reply within five working days and only refuse for operational reasons. More than two consecutive weeks needs head of service agreement.

Carry over: up to 5 unused days, to be taken by 30 June. Leave missed because of sickness or family leave carries over in line with the law and is not capped at 5 days.

Leaving: untaken accrued leave is paid; leave taken beyond accrual is deducted from final pay.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Sickness absence and sick pay
summaries.text:
Reporting: phone your line manager (not text or email) before 9:30am on the first day, say why, when you expect to return and what work needs covering, and keep in touch during longer absences.

Evidence: self-certify absences of up to 7 calendar days; more than 7 days needs a fit note from a GP or other authorised healthcare professional.

Statutory Sick Pay: from 6 April 2026 SSP is paid from the first day of absence with no lower earnings limit, at the statutory rate (£123.25 a week in 2026/27) or 80% of average weekly earnings if lower, for up to 28 weeks.

Organisation sick pay (includes SSP), per rolling 12 months: first year 4 weeks full and 4 weeks half pay; after 1 year 8 and 8; after 3 years 13 and 13; after 5 years 26 and 26.

Return to work: a short conversation after every absence; occupational health referral (with consent) and reasonable adjustments for longer or repeated absence. Health information is held only by the People team and never entered into unapproved AI tools.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Family leave
summaries.text:
Maternity: up to 52 weeks from day one. SMP up to 39 weeks: 90% of average weekly earnings for 6 weeks, then £194.32 a week or 90% if lower (2026/27). Topped up to full pay for the first 12 weeks after 1 year's service.

Paternity: a day-one right from 6 April 2026. Up to 2 weeks (one block or two separate weeks) within 52 weeks of birth or adoption. SPP at £194.32 a week or 90% if lower where eligible; the first week is paid in full by the organisation.

Adoption leave mirrors maternity leave. Shared parental leave: up to 50 weeks' leave and 37 weeks' pay shared between eligible parents; tell the People team at least 15 weeks before the expected week.

Neonatal care: up to 12 extra weeks if a baby needs neonatal care for 7 or more continuous days within 28 days of birth.

Unpaid parental leave: a day-one right from 6 April 2026; up to 18 weeks per child before their 18th birthday, normally in weekly blocks, up to 4 weeks a year, 21 days' notice.

Carer's leave: one week unpaid in any 12 months from day one; plus reasonable unpaid time off for dependant emergencies.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Flexible working
summaries.text: Anyone can request flexible working from day one, up to two requests in any 12 months, covering hours, times, days or place of work (including hybrid). Apply in writing through the HR system saying what you want and when. Your manager meets you to discuss it unless it can be agreed straight away. A decision, including any appeal, is given within two months. Requests are only refused for a business reason allowed by law, and the reason is explained. The Employment Rights Act 2025 will also require refusals to be reasonable; the policy will be updated when that takes effect.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Hybrid working
summaries.text: Roles that can be done remotely may be hybrid, normally with at least 2 days a week in an office or with colleagues, as agreed with your manager and team. Hybrid working is flexible, not a contract change, unless agreed through a flexible working request. Work in a safe, private space and complete the home working assessment; lock your screen, use the VPN on public Wi-Fi and never print confidential documents at home; be reachable during agreed hours.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Conduct and disciplinary procedure
summaries.text: Follows the Acas Code of Practice. Minor issues are handled informally first. Formal action only after a fair investigation; allegations and evidence are given in writing before a hearing. You can be accompanied by a colleague or trade union representative. Outcomes: no action, first written warning, final written warning or dismissal. Appeal in writing within 10 working days to a manager not previously involved. Gross misconduct (for example theft, fraud, violence, serious harassment, serious data protection or health and safety breaches, being unfit for work through alcohol or drugs) can lead to dismissal without notice after the procedure.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Grievance procedure
summaries.text: Raise concerns informally with your line manager first; if that is not appropriate or does not resolve it, raise a formal grievance in writing with the People team. A meeting is held without unreasonable delay, normally within 10 working days; you can be accompanied by a colleague or trade union representative. The outcome is given in writing, and you can appeal within 10 working days to a more senior manager not previously involved. Grievance details must never be entered into AI tools, including the organisation's AI assistants: contact the People team directly.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Dignity at work, bullying and harassment
summaries.text: Bullying, harassment and victimisation, including on the basis of any protected characteristic under the Equality Act 2010, are not tolerated. The organisation takes all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment of employees, including by third parties such as customers, service users and contractors, through training, risk assessment and reporting routes. If you can, tell the person their behaviour is unwelcome; report it to your manager, another manager, the People team or the confidential reporting line. Concerns are investigated promptly and fairly, and you are protected from victimisation.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Whistleblowing (speaking up)
summaries.text: Report suspected wrongdoing such as crime, danger to health and safety, environmental damage, breaches of legal obligations, cover-ups or sexual harassment. From 6 April 2026 disclosures about sexual harassment are protected in law. Raise concerns with your manager, the Speak Up Guardian or the confidential reporting line. You will not suffer detriment for a genuine concern, even if it turns out to be mistaken.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Bereavement and compassionate leave
summaries.text: Up to 5 days' paid compassionate leave when someone close to you dies; managers may agree more paid or unpaid leave. Parents who lose a child under 18, or have a stillbirth after 24 weeks, get 2 weeks' parental bereavement leave, paid in full by the organisation. Until the wider statutory bereavement leave under the Employment Rights Act 2025 takes effect, the organisation gives either parent up to 5 days' paid leave for pregnancy loss before 24 weeks.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Expenses
summaries.text: Reasonable expenses wholly, exclusively and necessarily incurred on organisation business are reimbursed if approved in advance. Claim through the expenses system within 3 months with receipts. Business mileage in your own car: 45p a mile for the first 10,000 miles in the tax year, then 25p. Standard class rail, booked in advance where possible. Normal travel between home and your usual workplace cannot be claimed.

summaries.title: HR policy summary: Data protection and use of AI tools
summaries.text: Handle personal data in line with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the data protection policy; access only what your role needs. Use only approved AI tools for approved purposes. Never enter special category data, casework, grievance or disciplinary information, or personal identifiers into an AI tool unless it is approved for that data. Check AI output for accuracy and say when AI helped draft a document sent to an employee or candidate. AI must not make decisions about people (recruitment, promotion, discipline, dismissal): a manager decides.
